subproblem.title: Radial cutoff fields h·γ(|x−ξ|)(x−ξ) are test fields (parent Step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, U ⊆ E open, h: E → ℝ with h ∈ C¹(U) (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h U), γ: ℝ → ℝ of class C¹, ξ ∈ E and a, b ∈ ℝ with a > 0, γ(t) = γ(0) for every t ≤ a, γ(t) = 0 for every t ≥ b, and tsupport h ∩ B_b(ξ) ⊆ U (B_b(ξ) the closed ball). Then the vector field X(x) := (h(x)·γ(|x − ξ|))·(x − ξ) is a test field in U (IsTestField U X): X is C¹ on all of E, X has compact support, and tsupport X ⊆ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (a b : ℝ), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h U → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → 0 < a → (∀ t, t ≤ a → γ t = γ 0) → (∀ t, b ≤ t → γ t = 0) → tsupport h ∩ closedBall ξ b ⊆ U → IsTestField U (fun x ↦ (h x * γ ‖x - ξ‖) • (x - ξ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra; B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the CLOSED ball; r = r(x) := |x − ξ|; λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_{(a,b]} means the integral over Ioc a b; φ' := deriv φ. This is Step 2 of the parent proof, for an arbitrary profile γ (the parent uses γ(t) = φ(t/τ), a = τ, b = (1+ε)τ).
1. (The set K.) Put K := tsupport h ∩ B_b(ξ). K is closed (intersection of the closed sets tsupport h and B_b(ξ)) and contained in the closed ball B_b(ξ), which is compact because E is finite-dimensional; hence K is compact (IsCompact.inter_left). By hypothesis K ⊆ U.
2. (X vanishes off K.) Let x ∉ K. If x ∉ tsupport h, then h(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so X(x) = 0. If x ∈ tsupport h, then x ∉ B_b(ξ), i.e. |x − ξ| > b; since γ vanishes on [b, ∞), γ(|x − ξ|) = 0 and X(x) = 0.
3. (Support.) By 2, {x : X(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ K; K is closed, so tsupport X = closure{X ≠ 0} ⊆ K ⊆ U (closure_minimal). Since K is compact and X = 0 off K, X has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).
4. (C¹ near points off K.) If x₀ ∉ K, the open set E ∖ K is a neighbourhood of x₀ on which X ≡ 0 by 2, so X coincides near x₀ with the constant 0 and is C¹ at x₀ (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
5. (C¹ near points of K.) Let x₀ ∈ K; then x₀ ∈ U. (a) U is open and h ∈ C¹(U), so h is C¹ at x₀ (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). (b) g(x) := γ(|x − ξ|) is C¹ at x₀: if x₀ ≠ ξ, the norm is C^∞ at the nonzero vector x₀ − ξ (contDiffAt_norm), x ↦ x − ξ is affine and γ is C¹, so g is C¹ at x₀ by the chain rule; if x₀ = ξ, then every x in the open ball of radius a about ξ satisfies |x − ξ| < a, so g(x) = γ(0) there, i.e. g is constant near ξ and hence C¹ at ξ. (c) x ↦ x − ξ is C^∞. Products of C¹ real functions and the scalar multiple of a C¹ vector field by a C¹ real function are C¹, so X = (h·g)·(x − ξ) is C¹ at x₀.
6. (Conclusion.) By 4 and 5, X is C¹ at every point of E, hence X ∈ C¹(E; E) (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). Together with 3 this is exactly IsTestField U X = ContDiff ℝ 1 X ∧ HasCompactSupport X ∧ tsupport X ⊆ U.
proof_key_steps: K := tsupport h ∩ B_b(ξ) is compact (closed subset of a compact ball) and K ⊆ U
X vanishes off K: off tsupport h because h = 0, outside B_b(ξ) because γ(|x−ξ|) = 0
tsupport X ⊆ K ⊆ U and X has compact support
Off K, X ≡ 0 on the open set E ∖ K, so X is C¹ there
At x₀ ∈ K ⊆ U: h is C¹; γ(|x−ξ|) is C¹ (norm smooth away from ξ, constant γ(0) on the ball of radius a about ξ); the product with x − ξ is C¹
Hence X ∈ C¹(E), i.e. IsTestField U X
